auxiliary_material: The study developed a meta-program (MP) scoring algorithm based on scRNA-seq data from mouse tumors to quantify TME remodeling, identifying myeloid-derived suppressor cell (MDSC) depletion as a hallmark of responsive TMEs. It established a resource (scIMD) and web tool (resTMe) for screening immunomodulatory drugs. The analysis covered eight cancer types for gene identification but performed in vivo validation primarily in the CT26 colon carcinoma model.
outline_action: Use this study to support the mechanistic plausibility of inosine-mediated ICI enhancement and to cite indirect human clinical evidence linking xanthine oxidase inhibition to improved survival. However, explicitly state that direct human TME inosine quantification and concentration-response correlation data remain unavailable in this source. Future search strategies should target metabolomics studies profiling human tumor interstitial fluid or tissue specifically for purine metabolites in ICI-treated cohorts.
remaining_gap: This material does not provide the absolute physiological concentration of inosine within the human tumor microenvironment (TME); the concentration data reported is from mouse cell culture supernatants. Furthermore, it does not report a direct statistical correlation between measured human TME inosine levels and ICI efficacy (e.g., ORR, PFS, OS). The human clinical evidence provided is an association between gout medication usage (as a proxy for inosine elevation) and survival, not a correlation based on quantified inosine metabolite levels in patient tissues or fluids. The study explicitly notes its limitation that drug scRNA-seq data were derived from mouse models.
useful_material: This study investigated the synergistic effect of allopurinol (AP) with anti-PD-1 therapy. In mouse CT26 cell cultures, LC-MS/MS analysis showed AP treatment increased extracellular inosine levels by approximately 500 to 1000-fold in supernatants, while cell lysate levels remained unchanged, indicating active export. Mechanistically, AP inhibits xanthine dehydrogenase (XDH), elevating hypoxanthine which is converted to inosine via the salvage pathway. In vivo, AP combined with anti-PD-1 achieved tumor-free outcomes in 4/6 mice. In a retrospective human cohort of 50 bladder cancer patients receiving anti-PD-1 therapy, the 7 patients concurrently taking gout medications (AP or febuxostat) showed significantly better overall survival compared to the 43 patients who did not. The authors propose that elevated inosine enhances tumor immunogenicity (upregulating MHC class I and PD-L1) and supports T-cell function.
